newsitem.title: USA: No frost risk seen for Brazil coffee - Smith Barney.
newsitem.headline: No frost risk seen for Brazil coffee - Smith Barney.

text.p: Brazil's coffee-growing regions should remain frost-free through at least the middle of next week, Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said Wednesday.

A cool air mass headed toward southern Brazil poses no threat to the country's coffee belt for this weekend, and there is no risk of freeze damage "through July 10 and probably longer", Davis said in his daily weather forecast.

While temperatures in the coffee areas will turn cooler at the weekend, dropping to the middle to upper 40s Fahrenheit (6-9 Celsius) on Sunday and Monday mornings in the southern states of Parana and Sao Paulo, these readings are well above frost levels, he said.
"The jet stream deliery will take the coldest pocket of air as far north as the Argentina/Brazil border (Rio Grande do Sul) but not up into the coffee belt in south-central Brazil," he said.

Davis said the absence of any kind of a storm system off the southern coast of Brazil -- a key factor in virtually every freeze during the past 20 years -- would protect the coffee belt from damaging cold.
Temperatures should begin to warm up early next week, he said, with no further cold fronts in sight.
